newsitem.title: USA: Trucking group CEO new US Chamber of Commerce head.
newsitem.headline: Trucking group CEO new US Chamber of Commerce head.

text.p: American Trucking Associations president and chief executive officer Thomas Donohue was selected Wednesday to head the U.S. Chamber of Commerce.

Donohue said he will press to expand the Chamber's financial and membership base, fight "unnecessary" taxes, regulations and government mandates and work to open up overseas markets for U.S. goods and services.

"Tom Donohue is well known as a forceful advocate for regulatory reform and staunch opponent of government mandates and higher taxes on the private sector," Michael Starnes, chairman of the Chamber's board of directors, said in a statement.
Donohue served as the head of the 45,000-member trucking federation for 13 years. Before that, he served for eight years as group vice president for development at the Chamber.
The ATA said that under Donohue's leadership, its revenue base has more than tripled, membership doubled and the fatal accident rate of truck drivers dropped almost 40 percent.
Donohue, who takes office September 1, replaces Richard Lesher, who has been the Chamber's president since 1975.
